# game.yaml reference

Every field of a game. Required fields are marked; everything else has a default. A game has the platform fields, a `round` of its mechanic, and the sections of its kit. A `kit: code` game has no `round` and no `theme`: its own code has the mechanics and the look. `gp explain <field>` prints one field, `gp validate` checks a file.

## Platform fields (every game)

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `spec` | `0` | yes |  | GameSpec version. Always 0 for now. |
| `id` | string | yes |  | Game id: kebab-case, also the folder name under games/. format `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$` |
| `title` | string | yes |  | Game title: the store title and the launcher label (Google Play: ≤ 30 characters). ≤ 50 chars |
| `appId` | string |  |  | Android application id (reverse domain). Required on Android channels; never change it after the first release.. format `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$` |
| `version` | section |  |  | Release version |
| `version.name` | string |  | `"1.0.0"` | Visible version. format `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` |
| `version.code` | integer |  | `1` | +1 for every upload to Google Play. ≥ 1 |
| `locale` | string |  | `"en-US"` | Language of texts and text-to-speech (BCP 47). format `^[a-z]{2}(-[A-Z]{2})?$` |
| `languages` | list of `en` \\| `es` \\| `pt-BR` \\| `fr` \\| `de` \\| `ru` \\| `tr` \\| `it` \\| `pl` \\| `id` \\| `ja` \\| `ko` \\| `zh-CN` |  | `["en"]` | The languages the game ships in, English first (CrazyGames requires English). The texts are in games/<id>/strings/<code>.yaml; the platform's own (host, kits, shop, dialogue, picker) are translated already. A portal game declares the ten its audience speaks most (W_I18N_LANGS): en (English), es (Spanish), pt-BR (Portuguese (Brazil)), fr (French), de (German), ru (Russian), tr (Turkish), it (Italian), pl (Polish), id (Indonesian); ja, ko, zh-CN are ready too. docs/guides/i18n.md. ≥ 1 items |
| `glossary` | list of string |  |  | Names that stay as they are in every language: the characters, places and the game's own words (the title always does). `gp validate` warns when a translation drops one (W_I18N_GLOSSARY); `gp translate` gives the list to the translator |
| `audience` | `ages-2-5` \\| `ages-6-8` \\| `ages-9-12` \\| `general` | yes |  | Who plays. Sets touch sizes and child-safety rules (`gp explain audience`). |
| `channel` | `android-families` \\| `android` \\| `crazygames` \\| `web` | yes |  | Where the game is published. Sets ads, purchases and policy rules (`gp explain channel`). |
| `kit` | string (kit id) | yes |  | Kit: the scenes around the round (menu, result screens) and the game.yaml sections they add |
| `theme` | string (theme id) | yes |  | Theme id: background, tap target, colors, pop sound |
| `saveKey` | string |  |  | localStorage key. Default: "<id>.save.v1". Never change it after release.. format `^[a-z0-9._-]+$` |
| `privacyPolicyUrl` | string |  |  | Privacy policy page (https). Required on Google Play.. format `^https?://` |
| `listing` | section |  |  | The listing texts the portal form asks for. `gp submission` checks them and writes listing.md with the form answers. |
| `listing.description` | string |  |  | What the game is, honestly (genre and the twist), what the player does and why it is fun — then a short feature list. Must match the covers and the video. ≤ 2000 chars, ≥ 150 chars |
| `listing.controls` | string |  |  | Every control, per device: "Mouse: …", "Keyboard: …", "Touch: …". ≤ 800 chars, ≥ 10 chars |
| `listing.orientation` | `both` \\| `landscape` \\| `portrait` |  | `"both"` | Screen orientations the game supports (the form asks) |
| `listing.tags` | list of string |  |  | Genre and tags for the form (e.g. Action, Clicker, Physics). ≤ 6 items, each item: ≥ 2 chars |
| `concept` | section |  |  | What makes the game its own, written BEFORE building it. Required where the channel reviews originality (CrazyGames rejected Petri Panic: "The concept is quite close to existing titles"). How to search the portal and what counts as a difference: docs/guides/game-design.md#originality-what-portals-reject |
| `concept.pitch` | string | yes |  | One sentence: what the player does and why it is fun. ≤ 200 chars, ≥ 20 chars |
| `concept.closest` | list of string | yes |  | At least 3 games already on the channel it could be mistaken for (search the portal by genre and tags, and the top of the category). ≥ 3 items, each item: ≥ 2 chars |
| `concept.different` | string | yes |  | What the player DOES here that none of them has: the core action, a rule or the goal. A theme, art style, setting or name is not a difference. ≤ 400 chars, ≥ 40 chars |
| `concept.twist` | section |  |  | The moment the twist happens in play. The game calls `host.twist("<event>")` right then; `gp qa` lets the demo bot play and checks it happens within `within` seconds (a new player must meet it early), `gp uniqueness` scores it. docs/guides/uniqueness.md |
| `concept.twist.event` | string | yes |  | Event name, kebab-case (e.g. "bait-feeds-swarm"). format `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$` |
| `concept.twist.within` | number |  | `30` | Seconds of play by which a new player meets the twist. ≥ 5, ≤ 120 |
| `concept.twist.explained` | string |  |  | The words on screen that explain the twist to a new player (the whole hint, or a phrase from it, as the game shows it; case and spacing are ignored), e.g. "your echo flies the dotted path". `gp qa` plays the first run with the demo bot and checks the text is visible — in the DOM, or in a host.qa canvasUi rect with `text` — before or when the twist first fires, long enough to read: 2 s + 50 ms per character of the text it appears in (≤ 8 s). Echoflies' playtest found its explanation on screen for 30 ms. docs/guides/uniqueness.md#the-explanation. ≤ 120 chars, ≥ 3 chars |
| `concept.progression` | string |  |  | What the currency or the run buys, in the shape that fits the genre: unlocks that change how you play (a roster of heroes or tools), tiers that open the next set, pacts (a gain with a cost), run choices (pick 1 of 3) — or a level shop, for idle and launch-distance games only. e.g. "Gems buy new candles, each with its own class power; feats are picked 1 of 3 at every level-up". docs/guides/upgrades.md. ≤ 300 chars, ≥ 10 chars |
| `story` | section |  |  | How much story the game has, and where it is. Optional: most games need at most a premise, and a game that needs none leaves this out. `gp story` prints the depth this kind of game takes and why, and forms a starting story file; `gp validate` checks the story against its depth (docs/guides/story.md) |
| `story.depth` | `none` \\| `premise` \\| `barks` \\| `chapters` \\| `branching` | yes |  | none: no story · premise: one line, who, what, why (≤ 30 words) · barks: a character reacts to events in a bubble (≤ 60 characters, never blocks play; 50–200 barks) · chapters: 6–12 short scenes unlocked by progress, played between runs, skippable · branching: chapters whose choices set flags that change later lines, 2–3 endings. Each depth includes the lighter ones. What fits comes from the audience, channel, kit and genre (the table in `gp explain story.depth`); outside it is a warning, never an error |
| `story.premise` | string |  |  | The one line the story is: who, what, why ("the pigs stole the eggs"), ≤ 30 words. It feeds the title screen, the covers and the store text. Required at depth premise. ≤ 200 chars, ≥ 10 chars |
| `story.file` | string |  |  | The story as data, relative to the game folder (e.g. story.ts): `export const STORY: StoryDef` for chapters and branching, bark lists (`export const BARKS = { event: [lines] }`) for barks. Data only (`import type` from @gp/core): `gp validate` loads it. Required at depth chapters and branching. format `^[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.(ts\|mjs\|js\|json)$` |
| `story.voiced` | boolean |  |  | Every story line is spoken (TTS or audio). Must be true for ages-2-5 and ages-6-8 from depth barks up |
| `story.genre` | `action` \\| `idle` \\| `puzzle` \\| `choices` |  |  | The kind of game, for the recommended depth (default: from the kit, listing.tags and the concept): action (arcade, survivors, roguelike, tower defense), idle (clicker, incremental, merge), puzzle (levels), choices (choosing is the play) |
| `money` | section |  |  | The money design, written with the concept BEFORE building: how long a session is, where its natural breaks are (the only places a midgame ad can go), what each rewarded offer gives, how long the meta lasts, why a player returns tomorrow. `gp forecast` estimates what it earns (ranges, with the confidence of each input), `gp validate` checks what can be checked against the channel. Every field has a default (the genre, the kit, the code, the balance report); on a portal a `kit: code` game writes it (the template has it as TODO). docs/guides/game-design.md#design-for-money |
| `money.genre` | string |  |  | The game's genre (gp catalog genres): the benchmarks (average play and D1 per genre on CrazyGames) and what its players expect (gp validate: I_GENRE_EXPECTS, W_GENRE_BLOCK). puzzle, idle, action, shooting, strategy, io, driving, hypercasual, kids, other — or a sub-genre, benchmarked as its genre: roguelite (action), survivors (action), platformer (action), tower-defense (strategy), deckbuilder (strategy), clicker (idle), incremental (idle), tycoon (idle), merge (idle). Default: from listing.tags and the kit |
| `money.hybrid` | list of string |  |  | The genres of a second layer the game has, on top of `genre` (an idle base under an action game, a rebirth in a speed runner: `hybrid: [idle]`). The blocks of that genre then fit (W_GENRE_BLOCK doesn't warn about offlineEarnings, Prestige or Sites); the benchmarks and the must-haves stay the main genre's. Genres or sub-genres, as `genre`. ≤ 3 items |
| `money.loot` | list of section |  |  | The game's random rolls (each LootTable source: an egg, a chest, a drop): what a roll costs and where its odds are shown. A roll for real money or for a currency sold for real money is refused (E_PAID_RANDOM: PEGI 16 from June 2026); a roll for a rewarded ad is a spin (W_REWARDED_RANDOM) — the ad gives a floor or a second item instead; odds not shown warn (W_LOOT_ODDS). docs/guides/live-world.md. ≤ 16 items |
| `money.loot[].id` | string | yes |  | The LootTable source the game rolls. format `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$` |
| `money.loot[].cost` | `earned` \\| `free` \\| `ad` \\| `purchase` \\| `bought` | yes |  | What a roll costs: earned (a currency won by playing), free (a daily egg), ad (a rewarded ad: a spin, warned), purchase (real money: refused), bought (a currency sold for real money: refused) |
| `money.loot[].odds` | string |  |  | Where the player sees each tier's chance before the roll ("the egg card lists each tier's chance"). ≤ 160 chars, ≥ 5 chars |
| `money.session` | section |  |  | One session as designed |
| `money.session.minutes` | number |  |  | Target minutes a player plays in one session (CrazyGames: Basic Launch compares average playtime; top games 10+). Default: the genre average. A code game that declares balance.difficulty.winningRunMin: `gp forecast` reads a winning run's minutes instead (the bot's, else the range's middle) and scales `breaks` to it. ≥ 1, ≤ 240 |
| `money.session.breaks` | integer |  |  | Natural breaks inside a session: moments the player goes on to the next run, level or day ("Play again", "Next level") — the only places `host.adBreak()` may show a midgame ad. The channel then allows at most one per 3 min (CrazyGames). Default: from the genre's run length (a code game without host.adBreak() has none). ≥ 0, ≤ 500 |
| `money.session.breaksAt` | string |  |  | Where they are, in words: "level end → Next level; death → Play again". ≤ 200 chars, ≥ 5 chars |
| `money.rewarded` | list of section |  |  | Rewarded offers (13+ only: never for children). Each is optional for the player — a same-size "No thanks" next to it (`gp qa` measures it) — never on the active play screen, and gives something the player wants. Default: the placements found in the code. ≤ 8 items |
| `money.rewarded[].placement` | string | yes |  | The id the game passes to host.rewarded() / rewardedButton(). format `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$` |
| `money.rewarded[].kind` | `revive` \\| `continue` \\| `x2` \\| `reroll` \\| `trial` \\| `hint` \\| `undo` \\| `boost` \\| `restock` \\| `spin` \\| `currency` \\| `other` | yes |  | What kind of reward: revive, continue, x2 (double the run's reward), reroll, trial (a locked thing for one run), hint, undo, boost, restock (a fresh shop stock now: restockShop), spin (an extra spin of a lucky wheel), currency (the shop's currency for an ad), other. Always a guaranteed thing, never a spin (W_REWARDED_RANDOM) |
| `money.rewarded[].gives` | string | yes |  | What the player gets, as the button says it ("Continue with half your wax"). ≤ 160 chars, ≥ 5 chars |
| `money.rewarded[].per` | `run` \\| `level` \\| `session` |  |  | How often it can be offered. Default: once a session for a revive, continue or trial (CrazyGames: a revive at most once per session), per level for a hint or undo, per run otherwise |
| `money.meta` | section |  |  | The progression's length. `gp forecast` takes it from the balance report when the game exports balance() |
| `money.meta.minutes` | number |  |  | Minutes of play until the progression is done (10–180 on CrazyGames: docs/guides/upgrades.md). ≥ 0, ≤ 100000 |
| `money.returns` | section |  |  | Why a player comes back tomorrow (Basic Launch reads D1: strong games 10–15%) |
| `money.returns.kind` | `daily` \\| `meta` \\| `story` \\| `social` \\| `none` | yes |  | daily (a seed, a case, a calendar), meta (a goal left at 80%), story (the next chapter), social, none |
| `money.returns.what` | string |  |  | The reason, in words. ≤ 200 chars, ≥ 5 chars |
| `money.removeAdsPrice` | number |  |  | The "Remove ads" price in EUR, for the forecast (kids apps on Google Play; the product is monetization.removeAds). ≥ 0.49, ≤ 19.99 |
| `sound` | section |  |  | The game's sound, where the code doesn't show it. On `channel: crazygames` a `kit: code` game needs music (E_SOUND_MUSIC): the code calls `createMusic` from @gp/core/sound — then nothing is needed here — or `music` says what plays (music code or tracks of the game's own). docs/guides/code-games.md#music-and-ambience |
| `sound.music` | string or `false` |  |  | What music plays, or `false` (with `why`) |
| `sound.why` | string |  |  | Why there is no music (with `music: false`). ≤ 200 chars, ≥ 5 chars |
| `budget` | section |  |  | The upload's size budget, raised on purpose (a physics, 3D or engine game). `gp build --target <portal>` prints the upload raw and gzipped, each npm package's share and the estimated time to a tappable Play on a slow phone, and warns above the channel's budget (CrazyGames: 400 KB gzipped, 3 s); this raises the size budget and the load warning with it. Never above the channel's hard limit (CrazyGames: 20 MB, which fails the build). `gp forecast` reads the size and the load time either way. docs/guides/code-games.md#the-size-and-load-budget |
| `budget.gzipKB` | integer | yes |  | Warn above this many KB of the upload gzipped (the channel's budget otherwise). ≥ 1, ≤ 20480 |
| `monetization` | section |  |  | Ads and purchases. Defaults come from the channel. |
| `monetization.ads` | section |  |  |  |
| `monetization.ads.enabled` | boolean |  |  | Default: true where the channel has ads |
| `monetization.ads.rewarded` | boolean |  |  | Rewarded ads (the player taps "watch an ad" for a bonus). Default: true where the channel allows them. A code game calls `host.rewarded(placement)` from the button's tap handler (or uses `rewardedButton()`); the YAML kits have no rewarded buttons yet |
| `monetization.ads.appId` | string |  | `"auto"` | AdMob App ID, or `auto` (filled in by `gp admob provision`) |
| `monetization.ads.interstitial` | string |  | `"auto"` | AdMob interstitial ad unit ID, or `auto` |
| `monetization.ads.limits` | section |  |  | Stricter ad limits than the channel (never looser) |
| `monetization.ads.limits.noAdsAfterLaunchSec` | number |  |  | No ads in the first N seconds. ≥ 0 |
| `monetization.ads.limits.firstAdAfterRound` | number |  |  | First ad not before the end of this round (or firstAdAfterSec, whichever comes first, where the channel has it). ≥ 0 |
| `monetization.ads.limits.firstAdAfterSec` | number |  |  | Or: the first ad once the session has lasted this many seconds, if that comes before round firstAdAfterRound (CrazyGames: 300). Only on a channel that has this time path; a game may only raise it. ≥ 0 |
| `monetization.ads.limits.everyRounds` | number |  |  | At most one ad per this many rounds. ≥ 0 |
| `monetization.ads.limits.minIntervalSec` | number |  |  | At most one ad per this many seconds. ≥ 0 |
| `monetization.removeAds` | boolean or section |  |  | One-time "Remove ads" purchase. Default: `{ product: remove_ads }` where the channel has purchases |
| `monetization.removeAds.product` | string |  | `"remove_ads"` | Google Play product id (one-time). format `^[a-z0-9_.]{1,100}$` |

## round — mechanic `tap-collect`

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `round` | section | yes |  | The round: mechanic and its settings. Everything except `mechanic` has a default. |
| `round.mechanic` | string (mechanic id) | yes |  | Mechanic id |
| `round.goal` | integer |  | `15` | Targets to pop to finish the round. ≥ 1, ≤ 100 |
| `round.maxOnScreen` | integer |  | `6` | Max targets on screen at once. ≥ 1, ≤ 12 |
| `round.spawnEvery` | list of number |  | `[0.45,0.95]` | Pause between spawns, seconds, [min, max]. ≥ 2 items, ≤ 2 items, each item: ≥ 0 |
| `round.prefill` | integer |  | `2` | Targets already on screen when the round starts. ≥ 0, ≤ 12 |
| `round.trajectory` | section |  |  | How targets move. `rise`: from the bottom to the top. |
| `round.trajectory.type` | `rise` | yes |  | Trajectory id |
| `round.trajectory.time` | list of number |  | `[5.5,7.5]` | Seconds to cross the screen, [min, max]. Slow for toddlers (5–8 s).. ≥ 2 items, ≤ 2 items, each item: > 0 |
| `round.trajectory.sway` | number |  | `0.15` | Sway amplitude, share of the target radius. ≥ 0, ≤ 1 |
| `round.target` | section |  |  | Target size: `radius` share of the short screen side, clamped to [`min`, `max`] CSS px (≈ dp). The audience profile sets a floor for `min`. |
| `round.target.radius` | number |  | `0.105` | > 0, ≤ 0.5 |
| `round.target.min` | number |  | `38` | ≥ 10 |
| `round.target.max` | number |  | `92` | ≥ 10 |
| `round.celebrateSec` | number |  | `1.4` | Fireworks after the last pop, seconds. ≥ 0.5, ≤ 5 |

## kit `code` sections

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `entry` | string |  | `"main.ts"` | The game module, relative to the game folder. `export default function start({ host, canvas, ui }: GameContext)`. format `^[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.ts$` |
| `background` | string |  | `"#000000"` | Page background until the game draws; also the browser theme color. format `^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$` |
| `engine` | section |  |  | The engine the game draws with, through its adapter in @gp/core/engines/<name> (created stopped, runs only while a run is on and the host isn't paused, resizes and routes sound through the host). canvas (Canvas 2D, the default: no package), pixi (pixi.js 8.x), phaser (phaser 4.x), three (three r163–r199, WebGL2 only). The engine is the game's own npm dependency: `version` must be the exact version pinned in games/<id>/package.json and installed; `gp validate` checks both and the adapter's supported range. `gp init --engine <name>` sets it all up. Kaplay is not supported. Physics (Rapier) goes beside the engine: `physics`. docs/guides/code-games.md#engines |
| `engine.name` | string | yes |  | canvas \| pixi \| phaser \| three |
| `engine.version` | string |  |  | The engine package's exact version, as pinned in games/<id>/package.json (not for canvas). format `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` |
| `engine.physics` | section |  |  | Physics beside the engine: Rapier 2D through the physics block @gp/physics (a world on the game's fixed step — the adapter's onStep — that stops with every host pause, is freed on every reset and gives the same floats for the same seed and inputs). rapier2d (@dimforge/rapier2d-compat 0.21.x) or rapier2d-deterministic (the same floats on every machine: @dimforge/rapier2d-deterministic-compat 0.21.x). The package is the game's own npm dependency: `version` must be the exact version pinned in games/<id>/package.json and installed; `gp validate` checks both and the block's range. It needs WebAssembly and adds ≈ 1.3 MB gzipped: raise the portal budget on purpose (`budget: { gzipKB: 1500 }`). `gp init --physics` sets it all up. docs/guides/code-games.md#physics |
| `engine.physics.name` | string | yes |  | rapier2d \| rapier2d-deterministic |
| `engine.physics.version` | string |  |  | The Rapier package's exact version, as pinned in games/<id>/package.json. format `^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` |
| `art` | section |  |  | Cartoon, game-like raster art made by an image model at build time and bundled with the game (never fetched at runtime: the portals forbid external resources). `gp art <id>` turns the style and each asset's prompt into a style board, then every asset in that style: sprites on a chroma key cut out to transparency, trimmed, sized and saved as WebP in games/<id>/assets/ with assets/index.ts (the imports) and assets/provenance.yaml (model, prompt, hash, date — `gp validate` checks it). The game draws the images and keeps the life in code: @gp/art lights, effects, rigs and the camera on top (docs/guides/art.md#5-generated-art-gp-art). Needs GEMINI_API_KEY in the environment. Finished pictures the owner supplies: `gp art import <dir>` (assets with `source: import`, no key) |
| `art.style` | string | yes |  | The cartoon look every asset shares, in words: shapes, shading, outline, palette, light, mood ("chunky cartoon crypt, soft cel shading, warm candle rim light, teal shadows"). Always stylized game art — `gp art` adds that to every request, and realism words are warned (W_ART_REALISTIC). ≤ 800 chars, ≥ 20 chars |
| `art.technique` | `painted` \\| `pixel` |  | `"painted"` | painted: cartoon raster art, WebP at the asset's size. pixel: pixel art — `size` is the sprite's grid in pixels (32, 48, 64: big sprites read better than 16), every pixel snapped to `palette`, saved as lossless PNG; draw it with drawPixelSprite (whole-number scale, smoothing off). A pixel game stays a pixel game: raise its sprite size and its ramps, never swap its technique |
| `art.palette` | list of string |  |  | pixel: the game's own palette (hex) — every pixel of every image is one of these colours, so new art sits with the old. ≥ 2 items, ≤ 64 items, each item: format `^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$` |
| `art.keep` | list of string |  |  | What the art keeps of the game — the game design leads the look: the identity that stays even if the technique changes (pixel → cartoon: the palette, the light, the hero's silhouette) and what play needs (what stands out at play size, colour codes for danger and loot, telegraphs). Sent with every request; the reviewer checks the art against it (W_ART_KEEP when empty). ≥ 1 items, ≤ 12 items, each item: ≤ 200 chars, ≥ 5 chars |
| `art.model` | string |  | `"gemini-2.5-flash-image"` | The image model (Gemini API). Default gemini-2.5-flash-image; gemini-3-pro-image-preview for the hardest assets. format `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{2,60}$` |
| `art.assets` | list of section | yes |  | The images, one per id: assets/<id>.webp, imported from assets/index.ts as ART.<id>. ≥ 1 items, ≤ 80 items |
| `art.assets[].id` | string | yes |  | The file name and the key in ART (dashes become camelCase). format `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$` |
| `art.assets[].kind` | `sprite` \\| `background` \\| `tile` \\| `ui` \\| `icon` \\| `keyart` | yes |  | sprite, ui, icon: cut out on transparency and trimmed. background: opaque, cropped to fill. tile: opaque, square. keyart: the cover illustration (the first sprite as the main character, the top third left calm for the title) — draw it in host.qa({ cover }) |
| `art.assets[].prompt` | string | yes |  | What this image shows ("the candle knight, three-quarter view, idle, holding a lantern"). ≤ 600 chars, ≥ 5 chars |
| `art.assets[].size` | integer or list of integer |  |  | The size in the game, in px: the longest side (sprite) or [width, height] (background). Default 256 for a sprite, [1280, 720] for a background |
| `art.assets[].from` | string |  |  | An existing image instead of a new one: a file relative to game.yaml (assets-src/…, from `gp assets get`) or a URL; gp art cuts, mirrors, trims and fits it, and for pixel art snaps it to the palette. ≤ 400 chars, ≥ 3 chars |
| `art.assets[].cut` | list of integer |  |  | With `from`: the rectangle of a sprite sheet, [x, y, w, h] in its pixels (`gp assets sheet` numbers the cells). ≥ 4 items, ≤ 4 items, each item: ≥ 0, ≤ 16384 |
| `art.assets[].flip` | boolean |  |  | With `from`: mirror it left to right |
| `art.assets[].upscale` | section |  |  | With `from`: made bigger with a pixel-art scaler, its design kept — `gp assets compare <image>` shows the methods side by side. xbrz (Zenju, the best on Candle Crypt), xbr (Hyllian), scale2x (EPX), nearest, or esrgan:<model.pth> (GP_PYTHON with spandrel); the result back in whole pixels in art.palette, small details (eyes, glints) kept pixel for pixel |
| `art.assets[].upscale.method` | string | yes | `"xbrz"` | format `^(nearest\|scale2x\|xbr\|xbrz\|esrgan:.+)$` |
| `art.assets[].upscale.factor` | integer | yes | `2` | ≥ 2, ≤ 6 |
| `art.assets[].upscale.keepDetails` | boolean |  | `true` |  |
| `art.assets[].redraw` | boolean |  |  | With `from`: keep the design, redraw it — the image goes to the model as the design and comes back at this asset's size and technique (a game's 16 px sprite as a detailed 32 px one, same shapes, colours and character), then snapped to the palette |
| `art.assets[].frames` | list of string |  |  | A sprite's animation: one pose per frame ("left foot forward", "both feet together", "right foot forward"), each painted from the sprite itself so the character stays the same, at its scale. assets/<id>-1.webp …, FRAMES.<id> in assets/index.ts; play them with loadFrames + frameAt (@gp/art/assets). Squash, bob and sway need no frames: @gp/art/rig. ≥ 1 items, ≤ 12 items, each item: ≤ 300 chars, ≥ 3 chars |
| `art.assets[].source` | `import` |  |  | import: a finished picture the owner supplied, made into this asset by `gp art import <dir>` (the plain background removed, trimmed, fitted, WebP; provenance `source: owner` with the original's name and hash) — never sent to a model, `gp art` keeps it as it is. `from`, `frames`, `redraw` and `upscale` don't apply |
| `art.assets[].part` | section |  |  | A part cut out of another sprite by `gp art import` (a car's wheel from cleanup.json `split.wheels`, its paint mask from `recolor`): drawn with its centre at `at` in the sprite `of`, in that sprite's pixels — assets/index.ts exports them as PARTS |
| `art.assets[].part.of` | string | yes |  | The id of the sprite it was cut from. format `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{1,39}$` |
| `art.assets[].part.at` | list of number | yes |  | [x, y]: where its centre sits in that sprite, in the sprite's pixels. ≥ 2 items, ≤ 2 items, each item: ≥ -4096, ≤ 4096 |
| `balance` | section |  |  | The balance as designed, before the tables: the session's length comes first (game.yaml money.session.minutes, entered by hand), then the one number everything converts into — the anchor — and the model (`balanceModel()`) is built in it. docs/guides/upgrades.md#start-from-time-then-the-anchor |
| `balance.anchor` | section |  |  | The genre's anchor: the one number the balance converts everything into (an RPG's time to kill and time to die, a sprint's distance over the session, a lap time, a tower defense's damage per wave for the budget, a roguelike's rooms a run, an idle game's income per minute). Declared, `gp balance` and `gp qa` fail on the model's first-session checks (the first reward within a minute, a new thing every 3 min of the first 10, no two big rewards in a minute, no hard streak, no jump in a stage's time, a goal in reach at the session's end, a meta of 2+ sessions) like on the others; without it they warn (W_BALANCE_ANCHOR on a portal). The model's `measure` should name it. A roguelite whose stages are a run's waves or floors says `shape: run`: the campaign's per-stage checks give way to a run's |
| `balance.anchor.name` | string | yes |  | What it is, in a few words ("clear time", "rooms a run", "income a minute"). ≤ 60 chars, ≥ 2 chars |
| `balance.anchor.unit` | string | yes |  | Its unit ("s", "m", "rooms", "coins/min"). ≤ 20 chars |
| `balance.anchor.says` | string | yes |  | What the number says, in a sentence ("how long one room takes a fresh hero"). ≤ 200 chars, ≥ 10 chars |
| `balance.anchor.shape` | `campaign` \\| `run` |  |  | How the balance model's stages are played (default campaign). campaign: a stage at a time, retried until cleared, the last one replayed for coins — the per-stage checks (no grind, no hard streak, stage time grows steadily, no stretch that plays itself) apply. run: a roguelite's run (waves, floors, rooms a run) — every attempt starts at the first stage and goes on until a loss, purchases come between runs; those campaign checks are left out and the run's are made instead: a fresh first run lasts 2+ min, the fully progressed player gets 1.5× as far (or near the end), a winning run fits the session, the runs get further within the first session |
| `balance.difficulty` | section |  |  | The difficulty as designed, measured by the bot skill ladder: the share of runs each skill should win from a fresh save, and how long a winning run lasts (Frankengun's targets: a skilled player — the owner's level — wins ≈ 4 runs of 20, a winning run 30–40 min). balance() reports the runs per skill (`skills: { naive, average, skilled }` or tagged `runs`: docs/guides/upgrades.md → the skill ladder); `gp balance` and `gp qa` fail a win rate outside the target ± tolerance (judged from 20 runs) and a winning run outside `winningRunMin`. With `winningRunMin`, `gp forecast` takes the winning run's length as the session (the bot's measured one, else the range's middle) in place of money.session.minutes, and scales money.session.breaks to it (forecast.md's Session row says so): the whole game is a run, and a player who wins plays it through |
| `balance.difficulty.naive` | section |  |  | The naive bot (a new player: slow, imprecise, no plan): its win rate from a fresh save |
| `balance.difficulty.naive.winRate` | number | yes |  | The share of runs won from a fresh save (0.2 = 4 of 20). ≥ 0, ≤ 1 |
| `balance.difficulty.naive.tolerance` | number |  | `0.1` | How far either side of winRate still meets it. ≥ 0, ≤ 0.5 |
| `balance.difficulty.average` | section |  |  | The average bot (the curve's player): its win rate from a fresh save |
| `balance.difficulty.average.winRate` | number | yes |  | The share of runs won from a fresh save (0.2 = 4 of 20). ≥ 0, ≤ 1 |
| `balance.difficulty.average.tolerance` | number |  | `0.1` | How far either side of winRate still meets it. ≥ 0, ≤ 0.5 |
| `balance.difficulty.skilled` | section |  |  | The skilled bot (a good human, the owner's level: tighter aim, quicker, dodges most telegraphs): its win rate from a fresh save |
| `balance.difficulty.skilled.winRate` | number | yes |  | The share of runs won from a fresh save (0.2 = 4 of 20). ≥ 0, ≤ 1 |
| `balance.difficulty.skilled.tolerance` | number |  | `0.1` | How far either side of winRate still meets it. ≥ 0, ≤ 0.5 |
| `balance.difficulty.winningRunMin` | list of number |  |  | [shortest, longest] minutes of a winning run (the skilled bot's median, else the best skill that won); also the session `gp forecast` reads. ≥ 2 items, ≤ 2 items, each item: ≥ 1, ≤ 240 |
